capture.final_message:
Use the representation \(\mathbb N_\infty \cong \mathbb N \cup \{\top\}\).

- A natural-number cast is finite, hence never equals \(\top\), proving the first conjunct.
- If \(n\neq\top\), represent \(n\) as the cast of some \(k\in\mathbb N\); then choose \(m=k+1\) to obtain \(n<m\).
- For the graph statement, any nontrivial walk starting at \(u\) must begin with an edge from \(u\) to a neighbor. Since `neighborSet u = ∅`, every vertex reachable from \(u\) must therefore equal \(u\); thus \(u\neq v\) rules out reachability.

Both sides of the displayed biconditional are consequently true, so prove them independently and combine them into the `Iff`. The essential ENat assumption is \(n\neq\top\), which permits reduction to an ordinary natural number.
